reviews.summary: Asked to cut two product plugs in the prose (the /dates date finder and the /long-distance tools), since VOICE.md allows at most two mentions, and replace them with tips a reader can use. Polish: 'film or show', a neutral word for 'housemate', check the mindbodygreen and YouGov sources.

All product, template, quiz, scheduling and link claims verified against the code; YouGov 38% and Chapman's ten-minute suggestion checked by search. Asked to fix the confusing 'two-phone games ... on the sofa' (EN and ES) and six Spanish lines: a calque-heavy ritual intro, 'tareas con la cabeza', 'mirándoos a vosotros', 'la mirada arriba', and two gendered words ('callado', 'liado'). Polish: the yougov.com/en-us URL, Picnic's first tap opens the lid, drop 'Many couples find', two smoother Spanish lines.

Asked to link 'receiving gifts' to /blog/gift-giving-love-language like the other three languages (EN and ES). Polish: put 'quality time love language examples' in the examples heading. All four People-also-ask questions answered; table, time ladder, ritual and mismatch section go beyond the top results.

applied: Date finder sentence replaced with 'Book it, or at least fix the day, before you tell them...' (EN and ES)
Long-distance tools sentence replaced with the fixed-slot tip (EN and ES)
Games line reworded to 'games for two, which work on one phone passed around the sofa or on two' (EN and ES)
Six Spanish fixes from the editor, as written
Polish taken: examples heading, 'film or show', 'share an address' for 'housemate', yougov.com/en-us URL, Picnic note's first tap, 'A good starting point is' in the FAQ, two Spanish polish lines
rejected: Polish not taken: a sceptical line on love-language research (no source read this run), bolding a 'tonight' pick, a number in the title, a quiz link in the five-types FAQ

reviews.summary: 10: the Counts/Doesn't count table, the ten-minutes-to-a-weekend ladder, a weekly ritual with lines to send and an honest gift section give a reader something to do tonight that the definition-and-list pages don't. Round one's fixes all made correctly. Polish: clarify the series row, drop the games clause, a research caveat, bold a tonight pick.

10: every claim checks out against the code or its source, round one's fixes are all in place, and both languages are specific and warm. Polish: 'Se cambia de día, nunca se cancela', closer Spanish for the games line, split the Picnic note's 'and' run, 'canceled' spelling.

10: it answers every People-also-ask question and adds a do/don't table, time-tiered ideas, a weekly ritual and lines to borrow that Calm, marriage.com and SimplyPsychology lack. Round one's link fix made in both languages. Polish: a quiz link in the five-types FAQ.

rejected: Final-round polish left out, as the rubric says: it goes in the record, not the post.
